highlights.title: Introducing Claude Opus 5
highlights.summary: Anthropic has officially launched Claude Opus 5, now the default Opus model in Claude Code with a massive 1M token context window. It runs in fast mode and is priced at $10/$50 per million tokens, making it a powerful upgrade for complex, long-context coding tasks. If you're tackling large codebases or multi-file refactors, this is the model to use.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.219: Opus 5 Default, Sandbox Network Allowlist & DirectoryAdded Hook
highlights.summary: Version 2.1.219 adds Claude Opus 5 as the default Opus model, introduces a `sandbox.network.strictAllowlist` setting that silently blocks non-allowlisted hosts in sandboxed commands, and adds a `DirectoryAdded` hook for automation when directories are added. The strict network allowlist is especially useful for teams who want tighter security around what external services sandboxed code can reach. Update now to take advantage of the new model and security controls.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.218: /code-review Now Runs as a Background Subagent
highlights.summary: The `/code-review` slash command now runs as a background subagent, meaning it no longer floods your main conversation with review output and correctly targets stacked slash commands. This is a significant workflow improvement — you can keep coding while the review runs in the background. Screen-reader accessibility also got improvements with announcements for deleted text.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.216: Sandbox Filesystem Toggle & Quadratic Slowdown Fix
highlights.summary: Version 2.1.216 lets you disable filesystem isolation independently via `sandbox.filesystem.disabled` while keeping network egress controls active, giving you finer-grained sandbox configuration. Critically, it fixes a serious performance bug where message normalization slowed down quadratically in long sessions, causing multi-second stalls. If you've noticed Claude Code grinding to a halt in long conversations, updating to this version should resolve it.

highlights.title: Claude Code Has a Hardcoded Instruction Telling Opus 5 Not to Use Subagents
highlights.summary: A Reddit/HN discussion surfaced that Claude Code contains a hardcoded system prompt instructing Opus 5 to avoid spawning subagents in certain scenarios. This is worth knowing if you're building multi-agent pipelines or relying on Opus 5 to delegate tasks autonomously, as the behavior may differ from what you'd expect. Understanding these internal constraints helps you design more predictable agentic workflows.

highlights.title: Claude Code Tutorial for Non-Coders
highlights.summary: This YouTube tutorial is designed specifically for people with little to no coding background who want to start using Claude Code. It walks through the basics of setting up and interacting with Claude Code in plain, accessible language. A great first stop if you're new to AI-assisted development and feeling overwhelmed.

highlights.title: Mastering Claude Code in 30 Minutes
highlights.summary: A concise 30-minute video that aims to take you from beginner to comfortable with Claude Code's core features and workflows. It's a time-efficient way to level up without committing to a multi-hour course. Ideal for developers who already know how to code and want to quickly understand how to integrate Claude Code into their day-to-day work.

highlights.title: Cognikernel: Local Persistent Memory for Claude Code Sessions
highlights.summary: Cognikernel is an open-source tool that gives Claude Code persistent local memory across sessions, so architectural decisions and project context you discussed last week aren't lost next time you open a new session. It goes beyond CLAUDE.md files by actively storing and retrieving session knowledge automatically. If you're tired of re-explaining your project structure every time, this is worth trying.

tips_of_the_day: After updating to Claude Code v2.1.219, run `/code-review` on a feature branch before merging — it now runs silently as a background subagent, so you won't lose your conversation context while waiting for feedback.

If Claude Code starts feeling sluggish in a long session with many back-and-forth turns, try starting a fresh session or update to v2.1.216+, which fixes a quadratic slowdown bug that caused multi-second stalls in long conversations.

When designing agentic workflows with Opus 5, test explicitly whether subagent delegation is happening as expected — Claude Code has internal instructions that may limit Opus 5's use of subagents in certain contexts, so you may need to use explicit prompting or model configuration to get the multi-agent behavior you want.
